operators.name: custom_equal
semantics: Corresponds to reference statement: equal = torch.equal(x, y)
Computes exact element-wise equality of the two input tensors, returns True only if all elements are equal and shapes match.
Inputs are CPU int64 tensors; no broadcasting, exact shape and dtype compare.
Returns a Python bool, not a tensor.

operators.name: custom_sin
semantics: Corresponds to reference statement: sin = torch.sin(x)
Computes sine of each element of input tensor x, with input on CPU int64 and output on CUDA float32.
The extension must transfer input to CUDA, cast to float32, and compute sin on GPU.
Output tensor has same shape as input, dtype float32, device cuda:0, contiguous.
Performs torch.equal on CPU int64 tensors x and y; returns True if identical, False otherwise.
Computes elementwise sine of input x, with x CPU int64 and result CUDA float32.
Output shape [16,2048,4096], dtype float32, device cuda:0.
Returns a tuple containing the boolean equal result and the sin tensor.
